name: Dense data
summary: Compact, exact and quiet, for analysts who scan alerts and compare signals all day.
description: Dense data is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Compact, exact and quiet, for analysts who scan alerts and compare signals all day.

ai.use_when: Security operations, threat detection, model monitoring, admin panels and analytics: many records, daily expert users, mouse and keyboard.
ai.avoid_when: Public sites, reading products, or first-time visitors on phones.

scenarios.text: A security analyst opens the alert queue at 8:00 and scans 200 rows for escalated threats.
An analyst compares this week's detections with last week's, model by model and column by column.

summary.text: Terse and exact. Say what happened and what to do, in as few words as possible.

principles.text: Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
Use numbers, not words for numbers.
One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.

inventory.description: The components this system carries, picked from the grammar catalogue by the components answers. Anything not listed is out.

in.why: Switches a table between views and densities.
Search with an icon and a clear button.
Narrows a filter to a range of risk scores by dragging.
Picks one value in filters and forms.
Picks one of two or three options, all visible at once.
Picks an asset or a user from thousands.
Lays out label, control and error the same way everywhere.
Keeps validation and errors the same on every record edit.
Notes on an alert, for the next analyst.
Picks a date range for reports and filters from a button in the toolbar.
The heart of the product: rows of records.
Analysts scan hundreds of alerts, filter by status and asset group, sort by risk and act on many rows at once.
Keyboard-first jump to any record or action.
Right-click on a row, for experts.
App navigation that stays open all shift.
A problem that stays on the page.
An empty table says what to do next.
Edit one record without leaving the table.
Experts size the table and detail panes.

out.why: Slides hide records; experts need them all in view.
A desk tool with a mouse and keyboard does not need phone drawers.
Hiding fields slows people who use them all day.

samples.description: Sample content for showing this system: written from its use scenarios, in its voice, with every status mapped to a meaning. Storybook, the site and the docs read it; it is never shared between schemes.

statuses.label: New
statuses.why: Not triaged yet; nothing is confirmed.

statuses.label: Investigating
statuses.why: An analyst is on it: news, nothing for you to act on.

statuses.label: Escalated
statuses.why: Needs a senior analyst soon, still containable.

statuses.label: Breach confirmed
statuses.why: Data left or an account was taken over: a real loss.

statuses.label: False positive
statuses.why: The detection was wrong; a finished outcome, not a failure.

confirm.title: Dismiss 3 alerts?
confirm.body: They leave the queue for good. This cannot be undone.

answers.question: business.q1
answers.why: The product runs daily security operations: alerts, incidents and the assets they touch.

answers.question: business.q2
answers.why: One internal product, one brand.

answers.question: people.q1
answers.why: The same people use it all day, every day.

answers.question: people.q2
answers.why: AA is the floor for an internal tool used by trained staff.

answers.question: content.q1
answers.why: Most of the screen is numbers and records.

answers.question: content.q2
answers.why: Experts want many records on one screen.

answers.question: tasks.q1
answers.why: People scan rows and compare values.

answers.question: tasks.q2
answers.why: The same actions repeat many times an hour.

answers.question: human.q1
answers.why: Losing your place in a long table costs time and errors.

answers.question: human.q2
answers.why: Daily users learn the interface and recognise it.

answers.question: outcomes.q1
answers.why: Speed on repeated tasks is the measure.

answers.question: outcomes.q2
answers.why: Acting on the wrong row is the costly error.

answers.question: brand.q1
answers.why: The interface must feel exact and trustworthy.

answers.question: brand.q2
answers.why: The data is the hero; the brand steps back.

answers.question: scenarios.q1
answers.why: Experts work at a desk with a mouse and keyboard.

answers.question: scenarios.q2
answers.why: The tool stays open for the whole shift.

answers.question: team.q1
answers.why: A small team keeps the system right.

answers.question: team.q2
answers.why: Features ship every month; the system must keep up.

answers.question: typography.roles
answers.why: A data role keeps numbers in aligned columns.

answers.question: typography.count
answers.why: A screen full of records stays calm with only the sizes it needs.

answers.question: typography.definition
answers.why: Lines stay on the grid so rows align, and grow with the user's text size.

answers.question: typography.values
answers.why: Small body text fits more rows on the screen.

answers.question: typography.lands
answers.why: Most text sits in table cells and inputs.

answers.question: color.roles
answers.why: Surface, text, action and status cover an operations tool.

answers.question: color.count
answers.why: One primary per view; the rest step back.

answers.question: color.definition
answers.why: One product, one brand ramp on cool neutrals.

answers.question: color.values
answers.why: Muted color keeps attention on the data.

answers.question: color.lands
answers.why: Color earns its place by marking late and failed records.

answers.question: spacing.roles
answers.why: Row height is a decision of its own in a table product.

answers.question: spacing.count
answers.why: A second, denser size serves tables and toolbars.

answers.question: spacing.definition
answers.why: A fine base unit gives the small steps dense screens need.

answers.question: spacing.values
answers.why: Compact spacing shows more records.

answers.question: spacing.lands
answers.why: Space is spent inside rows and cells.

answers.question: shape.roles
answers.why: Badges sit in columns and need their own corner.

answers.question: shape.count
answers.why: Control, badge and container corners differ.

answers.question: shape.definition
answers.why: One brand, one fixed set of corners.

answers.question: shape.values
answers.why: Small corners keep dense rows straight.

answers.question: shape.lands
answers.why: Corners show most on controls in dense rows.

answers.question: elevation.roles
answers.why: Only menus and dialogs float; cards use lines.

answers.question: elevation.count
answers.why: One shadow for everything that floats.

answers.question: elevation.definition
answers.why: Thin lines guide the eye along rows.

answers.question: elevation.values
answers.why: Subtle shadows keep the grid crisp.

answers.question: elevation.lands
answers.why: Menus and dialogs are the only layers.

answers.question: motion.roles
answers.why: Motion confirms an action; nothing else moves.

answers.question: motion.count
answers.why: One speed is enough for feedback.

answers.question: motion.definition
answers.why: A standard ease-out never draws attention.

answers.question: motion.values
answers.why: Fast feedback keeps up with experts.

answers.question: motion.lands
answers.why: Only state changes move.

answers.question: iconography.roles
answers.why: Icons mark row actions and status.

answers.question: iconography.count
answers.why: One size, matched to the small text.

answers.question: iconography.definition
answers.why: Outline icons stay light next to dense text.

answers.question: iconography.values
answers.why: Icons match the label so they do not outweigh it.

answers.question: iconography.lands
answers.why: Icons work hardest in toolbars and row actions.

answers.question: theming.roles
answers.why: One brand, so only the mode changes.

answers.question: theming.count
answers.why: Light and dark.

answers.question: theming.definition
answers.why: One product, one brand.

answers.question: theming.values
answers.why: Light first, always; dark ships as standard for night shifts.

answers.question: theming.lands
answers.why: A mode switch changes colors only, so layout never moves.

answers.question: accessibility.roles
answers.why: Pressed reuses hover; experts do not need more.

answers.question: accessibility.count
answers.why: Many statuses share one table; color alone is not enough.

answers.question: accessibility.definition
answers.why: AA contrast for every text.

answers.question: accessibility.values
answers.why: Mouse and keyboard; compact targets are enough.

answers.question: accessibility.lands
answers.why: Small text and thin lines in tables need the most care.

answers.question: naming.roles
answers.why: Components get their own keys.

answers.question: naming.count
answers.why: Primitives, semantics and component keys.

answers.question: naming.definition
answers.why: Role names survive a redesign.

answers.question: naming.values
answers.why: Lowercase paths read the same in CSS, JSON and Figma.

answers.question: naming.lands
answers.why: A component API keeps changes local.

answers.question: voice.roles
answers.why: Labels and messages are all the copy an operations tool needs.

answers.question: voice.count
answers.why: One flat tone everywhere; experts want no surprises.

answers.question: voice.definition
answers.why: A word list keeps labels identical across screens.

answers.question: voice.values
answers.why: Experts want short labels and short messages.

answers.question: voice.lands
answers.why: Errors and empty tables are where words decide the next action.

answers.question: components.roles
answers.why: Records need tables, filters and fast ways to move between them.

answers.question: components.count
answers.why: A full operations tool with the parts its next screens will need, still few enough for a small team to keep right.

answers.question: components.definition
answers.why: A component joins only when a daily task needs it.

answers.question: components.values
answers.why: Repeated screens stay identical when a component changes only with its meaning.

answers.question: components.lands
answers.why: Most work happens in tables and the forms that edit them.

usage.why: Titles stay small so the table starts higher on the screen.
Mono digits line up in columns, so values compare at a glance.
Help text is read in passing; body size keeps it quick.
Headers repeat on every column; a heavy style would compete with the data.
A light tint shows selection without hiding the data.
Red always means fix this, and the icon says it without color.
Links and buttons look different, so people know which one navigates.

usage.use: Badge with a subtle fill, an icon and a word
usage.why: Subtle fills let many statuses share one table.
Things that belong together sit close.
Lines separate without taking room from the data.
Compact rows show more records without scrolling.
Small corners keep dense rows straight.
Rectangles line up in a column.
On a busy grid, lines separate. Shadows blur the edges.

usage.use: elevation.overlay and a dimmed page for dialogs
usage.why: Floating things need a shadow so they read as on top.
Fast feedback confirms the pointer without slowing experts.

usage.not: A shorter version of the motion
usage.why: When people ask for less motion, nothing moves.
Experts learn icons; the tooltip covers the first uses.
Only semantic colors change, so layout never moves.
Keyboard users must always see where they are.
Compact still fits a mouse. Touch is not this product's input.
One primary makes the committing action obvious.
Cancel must be easy to find next to the primary.

usage.use: Button secondary, then confirm in a dialog
usage.not: Button primary as the first step
usage.why: Deleting is rare and costly; a confirm step catches mistakes.
Rows repeat dozens of times; a quiet icon keeps the table readable.

usage.use: The closest semantic token, then ask for a new one
usage.not: A raw value in the component
usage.why: Raw values break dark mode and the next redesign.

usage.use: One verb from the word list
usage.why: Labels repeat on every screen; one verb reads fastest.

usage.use: Name the record, then the fix. Flat and specific.
usage.why: Experts act on the message; the record and the fix are all they need.
usage.example: Alert ALR-2042 not saved. Threshold must be between 0 and 100.

usage.use: A short confirmation with the count
usage.why: Confirm and get out of the way; the next task is waiting.

usage.use: Why it is empty and the one action that fills it
usage.why: An empty table with no words looks like an error.
usage.example: No escalated alerts. Change the date range to see older ones.

usage.use: Name the exact object and the consequence
usage.why: Acting on the wrong record is the costly mistake.
usage.example: Dismiss 3 alerts? This cannot be undone.

usage.use: No tour. Show the data, with a tooltip where needed.
usage.why: Daily experts skip tours; tooltips cover the first uses.
usage.example: Hover any column header to see what it counts.

usage.use: a component from the inventory, composed (for example a popover with a command list)
usage.not: a one-off component built for one screen
usage.why: A small team keeps fewer parts right, and experts expect the same parts everywhere.

color.$description: Colour options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp and a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds). Steps only: each theme decides its own base (@). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

slate.$description: The slate hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

violet.$description: The violet hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

green.$description: The green hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

amber.$description: The amber hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

red.$description: The red hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

black.$description: See-through black for scrims behind dialogs, light and dark.

blue.$description: Blue ramp for the info status and categories. Same values as the accessible-first blue ramp: borrowed, not invented.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.
Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

16.$description: On the 4px grid, in rem so it grows with the user's text size.

20.$description: On the 4px grid, in rem so it grows with the user's text size.

24.$description: On the 4px grid, in rem so it grows with the user's text size.

28.$description: On the 4px grid, in rem so it grows with the user's text size.

family.$description: Font family options. Each brand's theme picks its display, body, interface and data fonts from these.

fast.$description: Fast: the usual convention for feedback, about 120ms.

moderate.$description: Moderate: a calm, easy-to-follow speed, about 200ms.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed: a slower, springy speed for expressive motion, about 320ms.

shadow.$description: Raw shadows. Elevation semantics point at these.

overlay.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in light mode.

overlay-dark.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in dark mode.

default.label: Dense data
default.description: The single brand: precise blue on cool grey.

theme.$description: The Dense data theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses blue, kept apart from the brand colour so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are violet, blue, green, amber, slate: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral slate.

default.$description: Height of buttons and inputs, and the smallest target.

container.$description: Corner of cards, menus and dialogs.

scrim.$description: Dims the page behind a dialog.

@.$description: Info text and icons: neutral news, no action needed.

category.$description: Identity colours for tags, labels and chart series. They tell items apart and carry no meaning.

@.$description: Category 1: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 2: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 3: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 4: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.
Category 5: chart series, tag dots and icons. Tag text uses color.text.primary.

disabled.$description: The shared look of controls that cannot be used right now.

text.$description: Text and icons of a disabled control.

focus-ring.$description: Focus ring color on any button.

icon-size.$description: Size of an icon inside a button.

border.$description: Border of a disabled secondary button.

checked.$description: Fill of a checked checkbox or an on switch.

background.$description: Fill of a dialog, menu or toast.

scrim.$description: Color that dims the page behind a dialog.

content.$description: Voice tokens: the words components use for common actions. Text, not CSS.

commit.$description: The label of the action that completes a task.

cancel.$description: The label of the way out next to the main action.

destroy.$description: The label of an action that deletes data.

retry.$description: The label that repeats a failed action.

empty-action.$description: The label of the action in an empty state.
